title: Minimize evidence burden: self-attestation workflow for enterprise contracts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales cycles are delayed by repeated requests for security evidence (CAIQ/SIG artifacts, screenshots, config exports). Customers ask for proofs that are time-consuming for our team to generate and for customers to validate. We want to reduce friction by enabling a trusted self-attestation flow plus a minimal, verifiable evidence option when required.

Objective: Ship a controlled self-attestation workflow in the Console and a lightweight evidence-minimizer playbook for Sales/SEs. Allow customers to sign a scoped set of attestations that map to CAIQ sections; optionally upload 1-2 pieces of minimal corroborating evidence (log snapshot, config export) if they cannot self-attest.

Scope: 1) Console UX for vendor attestations (create, review, sign); 2) Mapping layer from internal security questionnaire answers to the canonical CAIQ matrix; 3) Sales-facing small evidence acceptance checklist and templated responses; 4) Audit log entry for each signed attestation; 5) Guardrails and SLOs for manual review queue.

Out of scope: Full automation of CAIQ generation for now, bulk enterprise migration, and re-architecting KMS/HSM integrations.

Success metrics: - Reduce average security-evidence turnaround time from 12 business days to <=3 business days for qualifying requests - Decrease number of full evidence uploads by 60% in pilot accounts - Increase top-of-funnel conversion in enterprise trials where SE responds to security questions from 18% -> 28% (tracked per opportunity).

Acceptance criteria: - Console flow allows PMs/SEs to enable self-attestation for an account and customer can sign within the UI - Signed attestations produce immutable audit log entries (timestamp, signer, version) - Mapping from our answers to CAIQ sections is documented and exportable as CSV - Manual review queue exposes priority indicators and SLA metrics - Sales playbook and template responses are published and linked to the Console flow.

2025-02-12 - Miguel O: Kickoff with Eng (ENG-2145) to estimate work for audit log and signing flow. Eng estimate: 5 points for backend + 3 for Console UX + 2 for QA. Asked to split into two sprints; prioritizing backend and mapping first.

2025-02-14 - Legal (R. Chen): Confirmed self-attestation legal language required. Provided draft terms and change to default liability language. Added action: Legal to produce short-form attestation snippet by 2025-02-18.

2025-02-16 - Security (L. Morgan): Security review requested. Raised two risks: (1) risk of customers providing false attestations, (2) data retention of uploaded evidence. Proposed mitigations: signed attestations + audit trail + optional request for corroborating evidence. Security to deliver checklist and retention policy.
2025-02-18 - Design review: Mockups for Console flow (reviewed). Feedback: simplify copy, show clear 'signed' state, support exportable PDF. ACTION: Design to deliver final mocks by 2025-02-21.

2025-02-19 - Miguel O: Implemented prototype endpoint for creating attestations and storing signer metadata. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Backend unit tests added. QA plan drafted.
2025-02-20 - Aisha K: Sales enablement draft of playbook completed. Running workshop with SEs on 2025-02-25. Plan pilot outreach to 10 customers starting 2025-03-01.
notes: Implementation approach: backend stores canonical attestation templates versioned; customers sign via OAuth-backed Console session; system records signer identity linked to account. For high-risk answers, flow will require a 2nd-step evidence upload which is stored encrypted and subject to retention policy. Pilot for 10 customers, then measure metrics and iterate. Next milestone: complete legal copy and design mockups (due 2025-02-21).
